summary: the cases of the mount suite on i686, against kernels that time a request from its wait for a slot, never free a quarantined slot that is answered late, and let the raw writer open a mounted range

argv: ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh make rach2 && ARCH=i686 sh tests/proofs/guest.sh copy ${WORK} rach2/kernel

faults.name: deadline-from-wait
faults.summary: a wrong deadline: a request's period starts when its caller began to wait for a slot, so a request taken after a long wait is quarantined though the device answers it in time

edits.replace:
uint32_t wait_from = timer_now_us();
    uint32_t wait_tick = req_ticks;

faults.name: late-completion-kept
faults.summary: a lost release: a late answer to a quarantined request is dropped, so its slot is never freed and the kernel never says that it was

faults.name: claim-ignored
faults.summary: a missing refusal: the raw writer of a partition opens while the partition is mounted, so the claim probe writes its failure
